summary: Europa League and Conference League night. 28 of 54 games researched, 3 kept at medium: Union SG v Lech (Union win; rated low at first for missing facts, then medium after a full second pass with three bookmaker prices agreeing), Hoffenheim v Sturm Graz (Hoffenheim win, DraftKings agrees within 3 points) and Lyon v Lillestrøm (Lyon win; new coach appointed 9 Nov is a soft risk). Excluded: Beşiktaş v Hapoel Be'er Sheva (moved to Batumi, Georgia: neutral venue), Juventus v Omonia (every predicted XI has 5-8 changes and Spalletti announced rotation), Eagles at Cowboys (fierce NFC East rivalry), Frankfurt v Mannheim (fixture not verified, and a derby). Rated low, mostly because team news, lineups or a second price could not be confirmed this morning: Marseille (bookmaker consensus 9 points below Polymarket), Ferencváros, Sunderland (made 5-6 changes in its last home Europa League game), Salzburg, Benfica, Ajax, København, Brighton, Braga (still low after a second pass), Celtic, Monaco, Leverkusen, Atalanta, Getafe, Trabzonspor, Freiburg, Crystal Palace (new manager 10 days ago), Bournemouth, Milan, and the hockey games Frölunda and Skellefteå (no second price). CS2, Dota 2, the remaining hockey and the smaller Conference League games were not reached. The slip is three straight wins at 70-80% favourites, about 39% to land: negative expected value, bet only what you can afford.

checks.team_news: Starting11 (read today) lists nine Salzburg players out, including Boma (calf), Veratschnig, Tabakovic and Schmid (knee), Kitano (ankle) and Mellberg (muscle). Ararat-Armenia are without Bravim (suspended, red card) and Andersen (knee). I found no 25 Nov press-conference report from Salzburger Nachrichten, Laola1, Sky Sport Austria or redbullsalzburg.at (searches returned only older articles), and no confirmed coach-change status for either team.
checks.lineups: Only one predicted-XI source was usable (Starting11): Salzburg have kept 75% of their XI over six games and are rated 'Mixed'. Ararat-Armenia have named the same XI twice running (82% kept). A second lineup source was not found, so there is no cross-check and no official XI yet.
checks.rotation: Starting11 says a Bundesliga game three days later makes Salzburg rotation likely. I could not confirm the weekend opponent or the number of expected changes. Ararat-Armenia's last fixture was the 2-3 loss at Torreense on 5 Nov.
checks.motivation: This is matchday 5 of 8 in the league phase. FCUpdate showed Ararat-Armenia bottom of the table with 0 points and -9 goal difference after three matches. I could not read Salzburg's current table position. Salzburg's results look poor (0-4 home loss to Milan, 2-2 at Celje), so they need points. Neither team has a derby or fierce rivalry. The coach is unverified: a Nov 2025 article names Thomas Letsch and a later one names Danny Röhl, and I could not confirm who is in charge now or whether there was a change in the last 7 days.
checks.form: Ararat-Armenia: last five LLLWD, about 2.3 goals conceded per game, 2-3 loss at Torreense on 5 Nov and a 0-4 loss to AZ. Salzburg: 2-2 draw at Celje and a 0-4 home loss to Milan, with nine injured. I found no xG data and no Armenian league form.
checks.h2h: No previous competitive meetings found. Style matchup: a heavy favourite at home against a weak, leaky away side. Starting11's match model gives a 45% draw, which looks unreliable against the market's 9.7%.
checks.odds: Polymarket: Salzburg 85.6%, draw 9.7%, Ararat 4.6%. The 24h move is 82.5% to 85.5% (+3.6% relative) in Salzburg's favour. DraftKings on the ESPN scoreboard (read by the main task): -650 / +750 / +1400, total 3.5, which de-vigs to roughly 84% home. Starting11 shows 1.15 / 7.50 / 13.00 (about 85% de-vigged home). I did not reach OddsPortal or Oddschecker.
checks.models: Starting11 xGenius: 3-0 Salzburg, 88% Salzburg win. Starting11's other match model: 45/45/10, an outlier I discounted. I did not reach Opta, ClubElo or Forebet.
checks.venue_weather: Red Bull Arena, Wals-Siezenheim, kickoff 17:45 UTC (18:45 local), 26 Nov 2026. This is a normal home venue. I found no weather or pitch information, which is a missing fact in late November in Austria.

games.reason: I started from the market (85.6%), which Starting11's xGenius (88%) and the bookmaker prices broadly support. I moved 2.6 points from home to draw because Salzburg have nine injuries, probable rotation before a Bundesliga game and poor recent results (0-4 vs Milan, 2-2 at Celje). Confidence stays low because I could not confirm the coaching situation, the 25 Nov press conference, a second lineup source, the table, or the weather. The favourite's move of 3.6% is in its favour, with a plausible but unconfirmed explanation.
games.main_risk: A draw or narrow win: Salzburg are depleted (nine out) and rotated, and their recent form is poor, so they could fail to put away a weak side. The coach situation is unverified.

games.reason: Heavy rotation by Juventus, with 5+ changes from the 22 Nov Venezia XI in every predicted XI found. Venezia XI per Fantacalcio and Noibianconeri24 (same 11 names): Vicario; Celik, Bremer, Kelly, Cabal; Koopmeiners, Douglas Luiz; Zhegrova, McKennie, Alajbegovic; Kolo Muani. Today's Sky Sport XI keeps only 3 of them (8 changes), Quotidiano Sportivo keeps 6 (5 changes), Tuttosport keeps 4 (7 changes) and TuttoJuve keeps 3 (8 changes). Spalletti said at the 25 Nov press conference (per Tuttomercatoweb) 'Andremo a fare delle rotazioni carichi di fiducia' and that Ekhator will make his first Juventus start, with Como on Sunday the bigger priority. The coach has announced rotation and every predicted XI has 5-8 changes, so this is treated as a confirmed heavily rotated side. DraftKings -575/+700/+1400 (ESPN scoreboard) de-vigs to about 81.6/12.0/6.4 against Polymarket 83.4/11.3/5.4.
games.main_risk: Heavily rotated Juventus (Ekhator's first start, with Como next) fail to break down a counter-attacking Omonia side and the match is drawn or won narrowly, with a late equaliser possible.

checks.team_news: No Lyon press conference of 25 Nov was found, so this rests on previews. Lyon out: Morton (adductor surgery, back about February), Sulc, Ouedraogo, Mata. Openda is reported back by ruedesjoueurs but out by Starting11. Bidstrup and Tessmann are available per ruedesjoueurs, though Starting11 lists Bidstrup as doubtful. Lillestrøm: Garnas (knee) and Bassi out, Paintsil and Ranger doubtful, and Nyheim suspended per Starting11 only. I found no Norwegian-press coverage; VG, NRK and Romerikes Blad did not surface.
checks.lineups: Only predicted XIs were found, none confirmed. Lyon 4-3-3 (ruedesjoueurs, MediaPronos): Greif; Athekame, Bacher, Kluivert, Abner; Bidstrup, Tessmann, Tolisso; Duranville, Merah, Nakamura. Starting11 shows positions only, no names. Lillestrøm: Dahlberg; Ranger/Ottesen, Gabrielsen, Kristiansen, Paintsil; Ottosson; Va, Ibrahimaj, Kitolano; Gulbrandsen. The two sources partly disagree on Lillestrøm (Nyheim suspension) and I could not check the Openda and Bidstrup conflict further. Official XIs are due about 1 hour before kickoff.
checks.rotation: Lyon's last game was a 1-0 win at Lille (weekend of 21-22 Nov, inferred from 'le week-end dernier' in a 25 Nov article). Their next game is Ligue 1 three days after this one, and Starting11 flags likely rotation (64% of the XI kept over the last 6). A heavily rotated side is not confirmed, so no exclusion. Lillestrøm are in Eliteserien season (won last five, 3 games left per ruedesjoueurs) and also rotate (60% of XI kept).
checks.motivation: After 4 matches Lyon are 13th on 7 points (2 wins, no clean sheet) and still chasing a top-8 place, so they have a clear reason to win. Lillestrøm are 34th on 1 point (2 scored, 10 conceded) and need results to stay in the top-24 race. No derby. Carlos Vicens was appointed on 9 Nov 2026, 17 days ago and outside the 7-day window (a soft risk); Jorge Maciel was interim for 2 games and Vicens won his first game 1-0 at Lille. I found no coach change at Lillestrøm, though the Norwegian press coverage was thin.
checks.form: Lyon in Europa League: wins over Anderlecht and Crystal Palace, a 3-0 loss at Hoffenheim and a 1-1 draw at Real Sociedad. Domestically they are 4th in Ligue 1 after the Lille win. Lillestrøm in Europa League: home loss to Torreense, 1-1 with Sparta Prague, 0-6 at Real Sociedad and 0-1 at Viktoria Plzen. They won their last five Eliteserien games. I found no xG numbers.
checks.h2h: This is the first official meeting between the two clubs. The style matchup is a possession-heavy Lyon against a low-block Norwegian side. Lillestrøm have lost 3 of 4 league-phase games (one draw), and the Real Sociedad game ended 6-0.
checks.odds: Polymarket (06:51 UTC) has Lyon at 80.6%, a 2.4% relative drop in 24h from 0.825, under the 3% line; the likely explanation is rotation risk with a Ligue 1 game three days later, not confirmed news. Best prices on ruedesjoueurs.com are 1.19 / 7.75 / 13.00, which de-vigs to about 80% / 12% / 7%. Starting11 shows 1.20 / 6.50 / 12.00, about 78% / 14.5% / 8%. DraftKings on the ESPN scoreboard (read by the main task today): Lyon -475, draw +600, Lillestrøm +1100, de-vigged about 78.5% / 13.6% / 7.9%. Independent prices agree with Polymarket within about 2-3 points.
checks.models: Starting11's match model gives Lyon 45%, draw 45%, Lillestrøm 10% (tip: Lyon or draw), and its xGenius forecast is 55% / 25% / 20% with a 2-1 Lyon score. The two disagree sharply and sit far below the market, so I treat them as a mild warning on the draw. The gidstats, foresportia and oddscalendar pages were empty shells, and I found no Opta or ClubElo figure.
checks.venue_weather: Groupama Stadium (Parc Olympique Lyonnais), Décines, Lyon, which is Lyon's normal home ground. Kickoff 20:00 UTC (21:00 local); referee Sebastian Gishamer. No weather or pitch information was found, so I have no reason to suspect an issue.

games.reason: I started from the market (80.6 / 12.7 / 6.7) because independent bookmaker prices (ruedesjoueurs best prices, Starting11, DraftKings) de-vig to roughly 78-80% for Lyon. I moved 1.5 points off the home win into the draw. The reasons are Lyon having no clean sheet in the league phase, the 3-0 loss at Hoffenheim and 1-1 at Real Sociedad, a likely rotation with a Ligue 1 game in three days, a 17-day-old manager, and the Starting11 models showing far higher draw chances. Against that, Lillestrøm have lost 3 of 4 (one draw), conceded 10 in 4 and sit 34th, and Lyon are chasing top 8. The 24h move is under 3% and has a plausible rotation explanation. The draw stays well under 25%, but I am not backing the win over the market.
games.main_risk: A rotated, rhythm-less Lyon with a new coach (appointed 9 Nov) and no clean sheet this phase fails to break down a deep Lillestrøm block and concedes a late equaliser or one set-piece or counter goal, ending 1-1 or a one-goal win.

games.reason: Fierce NFC East rivalry (Eagles at Cowboys), which is a hard exclusion (derbies and fierce rivalries). The DraftKings moneyline on the ESPN scoreboard (read by the main task) moved from Eagles -120 / Cowboys +100 at opening to Cowboys -447 / Eagles +348, and the researcher found no dated news explaining it (search results returned other seasons' Hurts and Prescott injury stories that could not be dated to this week).
games.main_risk: Rivalry game with an unexplained large line move toward Dallas (about 30 points on the moneyline) and unverified quarterback status for both teams. A backup QB playing better than expected, turnovers, or a close game decided late could all sink a Cowboys moneyline at about 79%.

checks.team_news: Sports Mole (read today) has Sunderland out: Xhaka (calf), Brobbey, Ballard, Diarra, Mundle. Ta Bi, Ellborg, Browne and Alese are not registered for Europe, and Hume is one booking from a ban. Starting11 instead lists Hume as suspended, so the two sources disagree. Jagiellonia: Sports Mole has Sow doubtful and Wojtuszek back. Starting11 has Romanczuk suspended and Sylla doubtful, but Sports Mole starts Romanczuk, and my Polish-language search could neither confirm nor rule out a ban. I found no write-up of Le Bris's 25 Nov press conference after four searches, because Sunderland Echo, Chronicle Live, BBC Sport and the club site were not reachable or returned nothing. No Jagiellonia press-conference report was found in Polish press either.
checks.lineups: Two predicted XIs exist but they only partly agree. Sports Mole: Roefs; Meunier, Danso, Alderete, Methalie; Sadiki, Ahoka; Hume, Le Fee, Fofana; Isidor. Starting11 (early 4-2-3-1, partial) names only Roefs, Meunier, O'Nien, Methalie, Sadiki and Le Fee, and shows no Jagiellonia XI. Sports Mole's Jagiellonia XI is Abramowicz; Wojtuszek, Konstantopoulos, Vital, Montioa; Romanczuk, Klynge, Imaz; Agbonifo, Prelec, Szmyt. Nothing is confirmed.
checks.rotation: Last league game was a 0-0 draw away at Aston Villa on 21 Nov (Statz). Next league game is Tottenham (Starting11, no date given, and another page says it is two days after this match, so about Saturday 28 Nov). Precedent is a real concern: on 5 Nov at home to Dinamo Zagreb (lost 0-2) Le Bris made 5 or 6 changes (VAVEL says 5, ESPN and Sky say 6) after a 3-1 league loss to Coventry, with Chelsea named the week's priority. That is a recent rotation record. Press-conference guidance on changes before Tottenham was not found, so I treat rotation as a live risk. Jagiellonia also have an Ekstraklasa game two days after this one, so they are likely to rotate too.
checks.motivation: Table after matchday 4 (sky.de, 5 Nov): Sunderland 11th with 7 points, Jagiellonia 29th with 3 points. Sports Mole has Jagiellonia one point outside the playoff places at the halfway stage. Sunderland are in the Premier League relegation zone, which pulls priority towards Tottenham. Jagiellonia need points. No derby. No coach change found for Sunderland (Le Bris) or Jagiellonia (Siemieniec) in the last 7 days.
checks.form: Sunderland last 5 (Statz): W L L W D, 5 scored and 7 conceded, and they average 0.7 goals per game, 20th of 20 in the league (Statz). Gidstats: Sunderland home 2W 1D 2L, 2:4 goals. Europa League: W W D L, including the 0-2 home loss to Zagreb. Jagiellonia last 5: 2W 3L, 6:8, away 1W 1D 2L, 4:5 (Gidstats). Their Europa League run is W W L W L L and they lost 0-1 at Levski Sofia on 5 Nov. Ekstraklasa: 7 wins and 7 defeats in 14, ninth after a 3-1 loss at Cracovia (Sports Mole). No xG found.
checks.h2h: No previous meetings (Sunderland's first European campaign in decades). Style: a low-scoring Sunderland side against an open Jagiellonia side. Sports Mole predicts 1-0, and the Statz model projects Sunderland 2.5 goals to 0.7, which does not square with Sunderland's 0.7 goals-per-game record. Draw rate for this matchup is unknown.
checks.odds: DraftKings on the ESPN scoreboard (read by the main task today): Sunderland -400, draw +500, Jagiellonia +1100, which de-vigs to about 76.2 / 15.9 / 7.9. Polymarket is 78.6 / 14.7 / 6.6, so it is 2.4 points above DraftKings on Sunderland, within the 5-point band. Gidstats mirrors the Polymarket and Kalshi figures (78.2 / 14.9 / 6.9), so that is not independent. Polymarket moved from 79.5% to 78.5% over 24h (-1.3% relative), under the 3% threshold. No Stake or Rainbet price seen.
checks.models: Statz.ai model: Sunderland 76%, draw 16%, Jagiellonia 8%, projected goals 2.5 to 0.7. Foresportia, Opta Analyst, Forebet and ClubElo pages could not be read (403) or showed no figures. Sports Mole's text forecast is Sunderland 1-0. The Statz model agrees with the market but is not clearly independent of it.
checks.venue_weather: Stadium of Light, Sunderland, home fixture, 20:00 UK time, referee Georgi Kabakov. No pitch, weather or neutral-venue problem found, though I did not read a forecast. Jagiellonia travel from Poland on a short turnaround. A Polish report (flashscore.pl) says Jagiellonia fans will not travel to England because of a UEFA sanction, so the away crowd will be small.

games.reason: The second price now agrees with Polymarket (DraftKings de-vigged home 76.2% vs 78.6%), which removes one reason for low confidence, but the other gaps remain. I could not read the 25 Nov press conference, the two XI sources disagree on suspensions (Hume, Romanczuk), and Sunderland made 5 or 6 changes in their last home Europa League game, a 0-2 loss to Zagreb, with a Tottenham game two days later and the side sitting in the relegation zone with the league's weakest attack. I start from the DraftKings and Polymarket blend (about 77.5% home) and move home down to 0.74 and draw up to 0.19 for the rotation and low-scoring-draw risk. Away stays at 0.07. The draw is under 25% but the cushion is thin, so I rate it low and would not treat a straight win as a firm pick.
games.main_risk: Rotation before the Tottenham game, repeating the 5 or 6 changes made against Zagreb, combined with Sunderland's blunt attack (0.7 goals per game, Xhaka and Brobbey out), leading to a low-scoring draw or a late Jagiellonia equaliser.

games.reason: Neutral venue: UEFA's notice 'Change of venue for Besiktas vs Hapoel Beer Sheva' says Turkish authorities told UEFA the game cannot be hosted in Istanbul for safety and security reasons. It moves to Batumi Stadium, Georgia, on Thu 26 Nov 2026. Turkish press (Fanatik, Halk TV, Milli Gazete, Yenicag) reports the same. Some outlets say fans will attend, but a neutral ground in another country is a hard exclusion. Stage 2 and the coach-change check were not run.
games.main_risk: Neutral venue in Batumi, Georgia: Besiktas lose home advantage and crowd, and the 77% market price may not fully reflect that. This may also explain the 3.7% Polymarket drop (0.805 to 0.775), but I did not confirm that link. Reports differ on whether the game is played with or without fans.

checks.team_news: Hoffenheim are without Hranac (knee), Hajdari (meniscus), De Cat (meniscus) and Gendrey (ankle/fibula). Wimmer (thigh) and Conte are doubtful. Kabak was sent off at Frankfurt but is eligible in Europe. At the 25 Nov press conference Ilzer said everyone is available apart from the long-term injured. Sturm are without Khudyakov (leg fracture), Kiteishvili (calf), Rozga (muscle) and Grgic (knee). Koller is listed as out by one source and doubtful (illness) by another. Kicker, Ligainsider and Kleine Zeitung were not reached. These items come from the club site, Yahoo, OneFootball, Eurosport and tufutbolero.
checks.lineups: No official XIs yet. OneFootball and Eurosport predict Hoffenheim in a 4-2-3-1 or similar: Baumann; Coufal, Kabak, Machida, Bernardo; Avdullahu, Burger; Prass, Kramaric, Asllani; Lemperle. Yahoo has a back four with Rots and Daghim. Sturm are predicted in a 3-4-2-1: Helac; Malic, Quarshie, Vallci; Hodl, Weinhandl, Stankovic, Balbo; Seidl, Matoshi; Diakite. Yahoo has Petrovic and Heil in that XI. The sources agree on the core of both sides.
checks.rotation: Hoffenheim's last game was a 0-1 loss at Frankfurt on 21 Nov, and the Kabak red card is a Bundesliga issue only. Their next Bundesliga fixture could not be found, so I could not judge the weekend game. Ilzer said the squad is fit and accepted the favourite's role, with no rotation hints. The club site and Eurosport report no rotation plan, and a heavy rotation is not confirmed. Sturm lost 0-1 at Altach on 22 Nov, and their next league fixture was not found.
checks.motivation: After four matchdays both sides have 4 points, with Hoffenheim 23rd and Sturm 24th, so both are fighting for a play-off place and neither has anything secured. Ilzer and Prass are both ex-Sturm, which adds some edge but is not a fierce rivalry. This is the first competitive meeting between the clubs. Neither manager changed in the past week: Ingolitsch took over at Sturm on 29 Dec 2025 and Ilzer has been at Hoffenheim since Nov 2024.
checks.form: Hoffenheim won 3-0 against Lyon, drew late at Crystal Palace and lost 0-1 at Frankfurt. They have won their last three home games in all competitions but conceded in each of their last five matches, and their Bundesliga form is inconsistent. Sturm have lost their last three and are winless in six, with no win since 1-0 against Marseille on 22 Oct. They lost 0-3 to Bournemouth and 2-3 to Celje in Europe, and 0-1 to Altach and also to Salzburg in the league. They have conceded in each of their last six games but score regularly, with Diakite on 12 goals in 13 games. No xG data was found.
checks.h2h: No competitive meeting has taken place. The only known game is a 3-1 Hoffenheim friendly win in 2016. Both sides concede regularly, so a draw is a real but not the main outcome. Sturm often play open, so a high-scoring game is plausible.
checks.odds: DraftKings is 1.35 / 5.75 / 7.50 (opening 1.34 / 5.50 / 7.00), which de-vigs to 70.7 / 16.6 / 12.7. The 24h move is tiny, with Polymarket home going from 72.5% to 73.5%, which is not against the favourite. Eurosport on 25 Nov lists BTTS Yes at 1.62, Under 3.5 at 1.80 and Hoffenheim DNB at 1.11. Polymarket (73.7%) is about 3 points above the DraftKings de-vig (70.7%), so the two agree within 5 points. I could not reach OddsPortal or Oddschecker.
checks.models: No Opta or ClubElo output was found. Wincomparator's model gives Hoffenheim 58.6% but is based on only the last six matches, and Foresportia published no number and notes Sturm's form slightly favours them. Models that I found are weaker than the market, which supports shading the favourite down a little and raising the draw.
checks.venue_weather: The match is at the home ground in Sinsheim (SNP Arena, also called PreZero Arena) at 21:00 local time. It is a normal home venue, with no travel issue for Hoffenheim, who have won their last three home games. No weather or pitch problem was reported, but I did not find a forecast.

games.reason: I started from the market (73.7 / 15.7 / 10.7) and moved Hoffenheim down about 3.5 points to 70%, in line with the DraftKings de-vig of 70.7%. The draw goes up to 19% (DraftKings de-vig 16.6%) and Sturm to 11%. The reasons are that Hoffenheim are 23rd in the table, have conceded in each of their last five games and are missing three defenders. Sturm also score regularly, and the two clubs are level on 4 points and both need results. Sturm's poor form (winless in six) and Hoffenheim's strong home record keep the favourite clear. No manager change, rotation confirmation, derby or venue problem was found, so there is no exclusion.
games.main_risk: A draw or a narrow Hoffenheim slip: a thin back line (three defenders out, conceded in each of their last five) against an in-form scorer in Diakite (12 goals in 13), producing a 1-1 or a late equaliser.

Hojbjerg was ill and missed the Le Mans game, but he is recovered and was at the 25 Nov press conference. No suspensions (Le Phocéen, FootballClubDeMarseille, Eurosport FR). My searches returned nothing relevant.

Genesio signalled about 3 changes, not a heavy rotation, and Eurosport FR describes a thin squad after a summer with no signings. I found nothing on Levski's league schedule or rotation.

Levski are 10th with 7 points (2W 1D 1L), so they are inside the playoff spots and have plenty to play for. The top 8 is out of reach for no one. Bruno Genesio was appointed on 1 July 2026, so he is not a new manager. Julio Velazquez has been at Levski since Jan 2025, and I did not confirm his status past June 2026. Neither side has had a manager change in the last 7 days. This is not a derby.
checks.form: Marseille's last 5 per Eurosport FR: W W W W L, 11 goals scored and 7 conceded. They beat Lens and Leverkusen earlier in November, then lost the Le Mans game the manager called a 'phenomenon of fragility'. Genesio's own stated problem is defensive positioning and the reaction after conceding. Levski's last 5: D W W L W, 7 goals scored and 5 conceded; Foresportia lists their recent form differently. Levski have scored 4 and conceded 3 in 4 Europa League games. I found no xG and no home/away split.
checks.h2h: Only one meeting: Levski 1-0 Marseille in the UEFA Cup on 1 Dec 2005 (Eurosport FR). That is too old to mean anything. The style matchup is a Marseille side with a leaky defence against a Levski team with a clear game plan and a Spanish coach. Genesio himself said Levski play well and have good players.
checks.odds: Polymarket: Marseille 72.5%, draw 17%, Levski 10.5%. DraftKings now 1.35 / 5.5 / 8.5, de-vigged 71.2 / 17.5 / 11.3, opening 1.48 / 4.4 / 6. The price moved toward Marseille, with +1.4% relative in the last 24h, which is not a move against the favourite. GidStats' bookmaker consensus is lower for Marseille at about 63.8 / 21.3 / 14.9. Gainblers lists DraftKings at -222 for Marseille. Betclic (24 Nov): Over 2.5 at 1.54, BTTS Yes at 1.78. I could not read ESPN directly (403), so the DraftKings figures are from the candidate file. The independent consensus is about 9 points below Polymarket on the home win.
checks.models: I found no bookmaker-free model forecast. Foresportia and Wincomparator had not published a prediction yet. GidStats is bookmaker-derived. I did not check Opta or ClubElo.
checks.venue_weather: Stade Velodrome, Marseille, kick-off 18:45 local (17:45 UTC). It is a normal home game with no travel for Marseille. Weather and pitch were not mentioned in anything I read. Referee: Nikola Dabanovic (Montenegro).

games.reason: I started from the market and moved the result 3.5 points toward the draw and the away side. Marseille are 31st with 3 points and have just lost 2-3 at home to Le Mans, and the manager himself says the defence and the reaction after conceding are the problems. An independent bookmaker consensus (GidStats) has them at only about 64%, which is outside the 5-point band of Polymarket. Levski are 10th and unbeaten recently, with a fit squad. Marseille's confirmed absences are limited to two long-term injuries and the changes are about three, so this is not a rotation exclusion, and no manager changed in the last 7 days. The draw stays under 25%, so a straight win is still allowed.
games.main_risk: A draw or a Levski upset: a fragile Marseille defence concedes first or late again, as against Le Mans, against an organised Levski side that is in the playoff places and has little to lose.
